findings.issue: The LogThrottle 256-key tracking-set cap is enforced by a non-atomic Count check followed by Clear, so concurrent insertion of many distinct keys can transiently exceed the cap.
findings.summary: LogThrottle tracking-set cap is a defensive bound, not a strict atomic invariant; production keys are finite and never reach it
findings.detail: LogThrottle.Acquire does 'if (_buckets.Count >= MaxTrackedKeys && !_buckets.ContainsKey(key)) _buckets.Clear();' then GetOrAdd outside any global lock. Under concurrent distinct-key insertion the dictionary can briefly exceed 256 entries. However, in production the key is category + '|' + ArrTagsLogEvent, both code-owned and finite: 11 registered categories using a total of ~21 distinct (category,event) pairs, far below 256. The reset path is therefore never reached in production, and the per-key per-window emission bound (which is the actual log-volume bound) holds under the per-bucket lock. The test ThrottleTrackingSetIsBounded verifies the bound single-threaded; ThrottleIsThreadSafeAndBoundedUnderConcurrentAdmission verifies the per-key emission bound under concurrency. No material impact.
evidence: src/ArrTags/PluginLifecycle/ArrTagsServiceRegistrator.cs:171-185 (11 registered categories); ArrTagsLogEvent has 19 emitted event values
findings.recommended_action: None required. Optionally document the cap as a defensive bound rather than a strict concurrent invariant.

summary: APPROVED. Task 10.2 instruments all eight required boundaries (provider, matching, metadata, artwork, queue, reconciliation, webhook, lifecycle) through a new plugin-owned IArrTagsLog<T>/ArrTagsLog<T> facade that gates on the task 10.1 ILogVerbosityGate read from the current snapshot and applies one shared LogThrottle. Independent inspection of the full diff and all new files found no emission of an API key, webhook secret, SecretLease value, X-Api-Key/X-ArrTags-Webhook-Secret header, raw request/response body, provider DTO/payload, URL, or mutable PluginConfiguration: every emitted value is a Guid, a bounded enum, the non-secret connection identity, a configuration version, a count, a fixed bounded reason string, or an exception type name. ArrProviderError.Message is bounded to 512 chars and every producer (RadarrClient/SonarrClient/readers) uses a fixed constant, so logging it is within the ADR-020 clause 4 allowlist. There is no Trace-only branch, so raising verbosity cannot expand a redacted value. The registrator registers only ILogVerbosityGate, LogThrottle, and closed IArrTagsLog<T> types; it registers no ILoggerProvider/sink and does not replace ILoggerFactory, resolving ILogger<T> through host DI with ArrTags.* categories (NullLogger fallback when logging is absent). Log volume is genuinely bounded by the code-owned LogThrottle (5 records per category/event per 1-minute window, one bounded suppression summary on rollover, 256-key defensive cap) and the architecture.md section 12 limit row accurately records it. LogRedactionTests (65 cases) is meaningful and non-vacuous: it drives each boundary with sentinel secrets present in its inputs at all six verbosity levels, asserts no sentinel in captured host output with exact per-level counts, asserts Trace adds no message beyond Debug, and covers suppression, the window summary, the tracking bound, and thread safety. Independently reproduced: build 0 warnings / 0 errors; focused LogRedactionTests 65/0/65; full suite Failed 0, Passed 1363, Skipped 63, Total 1426 (baseline 1298/63/1361, +65). docs/limitations.md SEC-5 is deliberately untouched (task 10.3 owns it). Four informational/low findings recorded (stale pre-existing project-status suite count, an architecture 'durations' wording overclaim, the defensive nature of the throttle tracking cap, and the intentional SEC-5 deferral); none affect the acceptance criteria or block advancement.
